title: A review of the Effects of the Physical Components of the Interior Space of Architecture on Emotions with an Emphasis on Neuroarchitecture
review_question: Which physical components of the interior space of architecture affect emotion? What effect has their exposure had on neurophysiological emotion? And how do these emotions appear?
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Studies focusing on physiological variables related to architectural interior space or built environment interior space, using virtual environments (VR, CAVE, AR, XR) or physical spaces, and employing objective neuroscience tools (EEG, ECG, fMRI, GSR, fNIRS) and/or subjective self-assessment instruments (questionnaires, SAM, Likert scales, verbal responses). Excluded studies dealt with social, cultural, behavioral, or clinical factors, used two-dimensional images, were conducted on animals, or focused on 'affection' or 'mood' instead of 'emotion'.

findings.quote: Low self-assessment rank for pleasure and arousal in spaces with linear geometry and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) activity.
Arousal and aesthetic sensation in the curved and activation areas (ACC) (a region that responds strongly to the rewarding and emotional salience properties of objects).
Increasing the pleasure index of non-architects to curved spaces and the preference of architects to orthogonal spaces.
key_citations: Shemesh, Talmon, Karp, Amir, Bar & Grobman, 2017

findings.consequent: arousal ranks, heart rate, theta power
findings.quote: Higher arousal ranks in furnished spaces and increased heart rate and greater theta power in the space.
key_citations: Vecchiato, Tieri, Jelic, De Matteis, Maglione & Babiloni, 2015b
Vecchiato et, Jelic, Tieri, Maglione, Matteis & Babiloni, 2015a

findings.consequent: stress and fatigue, physiological setting and ease
findings.quote: Less stress and fatigue in rooms with wood design, and physiological setting and ease.

findings.consequent: sense of pleasure, perception of beauty, decision to leave the space
findings.quote: Decreasing the sense of pleasure and perception of beauty in closed rooms with low ceilings and the decision to leave the space.

findings.antecedent: Doors with medium and large width
findings.quote: Arousal in front of doors with medium and large width.
Reducing the level of physiological indicators of stress in the outdoors towards nature and increasing creativity.
key_citations: Yin, Arfaei, MacNaughton, Catalano, Allen & Spengler, 2019

synthesis_conclusions: Curved forms in interior architectural design increase anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) activity, inducing feelings of pleasure, arousal, relaxation, and beauty.
Architects prefer orthogonal spaces, while non-architects prefer curved spaces.
The use of wood texture in interior design reduces tension and fatigue, adjusts physiological responses, and leads to feelings of relaxation and arousal.
Spaces with furniture increase heart rate and theta power, indicating an effect on human emotions.
Rooms with low ceiling height and indoors induce feelings of disgust and a decision to leave, whereas higher ceilings and outdoor environments evoke pleasure.
Connecting with nature through openings reduces fatigue and increases creativity, serving as an important criterion for healthy interior design.
evidence_gaps: Lack of investigation into objective components such as color and light.
Lack of investigation into mental components such as the sense of belonging and the sense of place.
heterogeneity_sources: Different methods and instruments to measure emotion across studies.
limitations: Emerging nature of the field leading to methodological challenges.
Inability to define a specific, repeatable framework due to varied methods and instruments.
Small and limited statistical populations, restricting generalizability.
Diverse methods of information analysis requiring further experiments for validation.
